sections.heading: A planned outreach with a security dimension
paragraphs: The Press Information Bureau records that Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to meet, on 20 October 2026, families in Mansa, Sangrur and Gurdaspur whose members lost their lives after speaking against “chitta” (synthetic drug) traders. The practical consequence is national-level attention to families associated with alleged drug-linked intimidation.

The source does not establish that the meetings themselves will produce arrests, nor does it provide case files, legal provisions, medical evidence or conviction data. A visit should therefore be understood as outreach and signalling, not proof of enforcement success.

sections.heading: From public health to internal security
paragraphs: The mechanism is straightforward: when an illicit trade is accompanied by threats or lethal retaliation, residents may stop reporting networks and cooperating with investigators. That can reduce trust in institutions and strengthen criminal impunity. An effective response must consequently combine protection and impartial investigation with prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.

For UPSC analysis, the issue also tests cooperative federalism. Union-level attention cannot substitute for lawful state-level investigation or accountable prosecution, while state action can benefit from coordinated support where criminal networks cross jurisdictions.
